texts.preamble: Dambaru Dhar Mishra And Another vs State Of Odisha And Others .... Opp. ... on 14 September, 2021 Author: K.R. Mohapatra Bench: K.R. Mohapatra In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack W.P.(C) No.27723 of 2021 Dambaru Dhar Mishra and another .... Petitioners Mr.Sanjit Kumar Das, Advocate -versus- State of Odisha and others .... Opp. Parties Mr.Bibhudhendra Dash, Advocate (For Opposite Party Nos.3 and 4) Coram: Justice K.R. Mohapatra Order Order No. 14.09.2021 3. 1.
texts.arguments: 2. Petitioner, in this writ petition, seeks to assail the action of the Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC) in taking coercive measure for eviction of their shops situated at Bhimatangi Chhak, Ward Nos.60 and 61, Bhimatangi Housing Board, Bhubaneswar in the district of Khordha of the Petitioners. 3. It is submitted by Mr. Das, learned counsel for the Petitioners that the Petitioners are running their shops covering Ward Nos. 60 and 61 of Bhimatangi Chhak. Although they are street vendors as per the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014 (for short, 'the Act') no survey has yet been made by the BMC authority in consonance with Sections 3 and 18 of the Act. Further, they are identified and issued with certificate-cum-letter of recommendation and registration certificate by the Health and Family Welfare Department Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Certificate of Registration under FSS Act, 2006 and they have been issued with ID cards from time to time valid up to 6th February, 2023. However, in spite of all these, BMC authorities // 2 // are threatening to evict and demolish the shop of the Petitioner without issuing any notice to the Petitioners. It is submitted that law is well-settled that even a trespasser cannot be evicted without following due procedure of law. Finding no other alternative, the Petitioners have approached this Court by filing the present writ petition. 5. Mr. Dash, learned Counsel for the BMC submits that since the Petitioners allege coercive action by the BMC, they may approach the appropriate authority of the BMC for redressal of their grievances.
